name: Roman-style stone town wall ring, 3/4 top-down (16px tiles): walkable wall-walk tops seen from above with crenellated parapets, the front faces of the north and south walls below them, a gatehouse with an open round arch (passage), a gatehouse with closed wooden doors, square towers with terracotta tiled pyramid roofs, stone stairs up the inner face, a gap in the west wall

answer.evidence: The towers have sloped terracotta pyramid roofs (rows 0-31 and 150-175) whose tile rows form the top plane. The gatehouses have crenellated platforms (about rows 32-47 and 176-191) that end in an edge line and are followed by stone front faces. The north and south walls show a walk-top band with a crenellated parapet (rows ~49-62 and ~192-201). Below each band is a front face of about 33 rows (rows ~63-95), with stairs, arch and doors drawn on it. The east wall shows its walk-top from above. Every major part has a top surface above a front face, so the drawing matches the right-hand references and the synthetic cabinet 'top 5 + edge + eave'.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is clean and coherent. Stone walls have 3-4 value steps (light mortar, light/mid/dark block faces), with per-brick shading and a few cross-shaped slit and torch details. The tile roofs on the towers show about 3-4 terracotta steps, but they are small and fairly smooth, without the per-tile highlight scallops of the reference roofs. Outlines are dark purple-blue/brown tinted, not neutral black (15% neutral edge share, against 7-9% for the references), so they read as material-tone. Measured density is 8 visible tones per tile against 10-12 for the references, which is lower but not far below, and near-flat coverage is 1% (no large flat fills). The stone is modestly textured with no speckle or grain on the blocks, and the wall-walk tops are plain pale bands. The grey cobble patches are a flat dithered noise pattern. Overall it is a bit shallower than the references in ramp depth and texture, and a careful artist would notice it looks thinner next to house-h101. When in doubt, fail.

answer.evidence: Pyramid roofs (rows 0-31) have tile slopes whose width grows from 32 to 62 and end in an eave edge at row 31. The gatehouse (rows 32-47) and the north wall (rows 48-60) each have a crenellated walkway top with a front-edge line and a shadow row beneath, followed by a stone-brick front face of about 35 rows (rows 61-95 in column x=68, with the brick course repeating every 16 rows). The south wall and gatehouse repeat this structure in rows 176-239. The east wall-walk is drawn as a horizontal surface seen from above. The stairs, doors and arch are vertical details on the front faces, so no major part is missing its top.

styleAnswer.evidence: The outlines are a dark purple-brown tint, not neutral black (15% near-neutral edge pixels against 7-9% in the references). That matches the Beodeul approach, and near-flat coverage is 1%, so there are no real flat fills. Against that, the candidate shows 8 visible tones per tile against 10-12 in the references, and the shading is shallower. Stone blocks get roughly 4 steps (highlight edge, light, mid, dark joint), where the references use about 6. The terracotta pyramid roofs are small and smooth, with 3-4 reds and none of the per-tile scallops and highlights seen on the reference roofs. The wall faces repeat one block pattern with little per-stone variation or speckle. The wooden door has good grain and the cobble patches are textured, but the overall result looks cleaner and flatter than the references. Since it would read as thinner next to them, it fails.

answer.evidence: The north wall (x=136 column) has a top band at rows 48-60: a light parapet at rows 49-52, an edge line at rows 53-54, and darker shadow at rows 59-60. A stone front face of about 35 rows follows, ending at row 95. The gatehouses show crenellated platform tops (rows 32-47 and 176-191) above their front faces. The square towers have sloped terracotta tile pyramid roofs (rows 7-35 and 150-179) above their stone shafts. The wall-walks of the east and west walls are seen from above. The gatehouse doors and arch are vertical faces, as expected. All major parts show a top surface plus a front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 8 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 in the references, so it sits slightly below them. Near-flat coverage is 1%, so there are no big flat fills, and the stone blocks carry per-brick variation. The dark edge pixels are only 15% neutral, so the outline leans purple or blue-brown, a dark tone of the stone, and is not a sticker line. Shading is shallower than the references. The stone ramp has about 4 steps (highlight, light, mid, dark mortar), and the terracotta roofs on the towers have about 3-4 steps with little per-tile scallop detail. The references show 5-6 steps with tile-by-tile highlights, plaster speckle and grain. The wall-walk tops and large wall faces repeat the same brick pattern with little grain, and the cobble patches are noisy but uniform. The piece is cleanly drawn and sits near the references, but it reads a little thinner and flatter. When in doubt, fail.

answer.evidence: The gatehouses have crenellated wall-walk tops (rows 32-47 north, 176-191 south) that end in an edge line with a shadow. A tall stone front face sits below them (rows 48-95 north, 192-239 south). The towers have sloped terracotta pyramid roofs (rows 0-31, 150-179), which count as top surfaces, above their stone front faces. The north and east walls show walk tops with parapets above their front faces. The west wall has a gap, which does not change the reading. The arch passage and the wooden doors are vertical faces, which is normal. Every major part has a top surface and a front face of 3 or more rows.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 8 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 for the references, which is slightly lower but not far off. Near-flat coverage is 1%, so there are no big flat areas. Dark edge pixels are only 15% neutral, and the outlines lean purple-brown or blue-grey, so they read as tinted material tone rather than a black sticker line. The stone walls have per-block shading with some speckle, but each block is shaded with only about 3-4 steps. The terracotta tower roofs are small and have only 3-4 tones, with none of the per-tile scallop highlights the references show. The wall-walk tops and the large paved patches are fairly uniform. The wooden door is well shaded, with planks and iron bands. Overall it is clean and competent but a bit shallower in ramp depth and texture than Beodeul, and the reference roofs are noticeably richer. When in doubt, fail.
